Hi Alex — thanks for the heads up. I saw the forwarded invite thread and the same issue popped up for one of our SEs in Singapore last time someone forwarded an invite without TZ data.

Quick notes / proposal:
- Google Calendar sometimes treats invites as 'floating' if the ICS doesn't include an explicit VTIMEZONE block. That makes forwarded copies appear in the recipient's local time without applying the original offset.
- To avoid this, I'll create and attach a Redwood-generated .ics that includes explicit VTIMEZONE entries and send a replacement invite with the time noted in UTC and local equivalents.
- Alternate option: schedule in UTC (we'll propose 18:00 UTC / 10:00 PT / 03:00 JST) and include that as the event title and description so attendees see the UTC anchor regardless of forwarding.

I'm looping in Marissa (SE) and Stephanie (Regional AM) to confirm availability and to set a new invite that pins timezone info.

Attaching: redwood-demo-ics.ics (contains VTIMEZONE for PST/UTC/JST)

Best,

Good call on an explicit VTIMEZONE .ics. APAC customers often use non-Google clients that strip the anchor. When I set up multi-region calls I also add the UTC time to the event title like: "Redwood demo — 18:00 UTC / 10:00 PT / 03:00 JST". That way even if the invite floats the title shows the canonical time.
